key_insight: An attention-fused TFT–N-BEATS model jointly forecasts PV power across five horizons, with reported RMSE reductions of 35–40% versus TFT.
engineering_relevance: Multi-horizon forecasts could support grid scheduling and PV–battery operation, while attention and trend–seasonality views aid interpretation.
method: TFT models short-term dependencies and dynamic feature importance.
N-BEATS decomposes longer-term trends and seasonality.
Adaptive attention fuses both branches for 30-minute, 2-hour, 6-hour, 12-hour, and 24-hour forecasts.
evidence_signal: On multi-year DKASC datasets, the abstract reports RMSE values of 42.35–52.29 and MAPE below 5%; RMSE units and horizon-specific results are not provided.
watch_item: Generalization beyond DKASC remains unestablished; this is PV power forecasting research, not a perovskite cell-materials study.
paper_title: A Hybrid TFT-NBEATS Framework for Robust Multi-Horizon Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
